title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 166
paragraphs: This Aryandes had been appointed governor of the province of Egypt by Cambyses; and after the events here described he lost his life because he tried to measure himself against Darius. For having heard and seen that Darius wanted to leave behind him as a memorial something no other king had ever made, he imitated him—until at last he got his reward. For whereas Darius refined gold and made it as pure as possible, and had coins struck from it, Aryandes, being ruler of Egypt, did the same thing with silver; and even now the purest silver is what is called Aryandic. When Darius learned that he was doing this, he put him to death, bringing against him another charge—that of attempting rebellion.
